transcript.content: Hi, welcome in, I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, Doc. Well, I guess my work physical is what got me here. The doctor doing the exam told me my weight is too low. I don't really see the issue, honestly. To me, I just feel... lighter on my feet when I play basketball, and I'm not as weighed down when I'm moving around the garage.
Do you find yourself limiting how much you eat, or feeling anxious about gaining weight?

Well, yeah, I suppose I do limit it. Most days I just keep it to coffee in the morning. Then later on, maybe I'll have a small sandwich or just half of whatever's around. The shop is usually running late, and things are always busy at the house, so... I just feel better sticking to my own simple rules. It just keeps things manageable for me, you know?
Even though your doctor said you're underweight, do you ever worry about gaining weight or see yourself as heavier than you actually are?

Yeah, I do worry about it. I mean... if I see the scale bump up even a pound, or if my work jeans start to feel tighter, I just start thinking I'm getting soft. It bothers me. I worry that I'll end up being slower moving around the cars at the shop, or... or slower getting up and down the court. So, yeah, I definitely don't want to put weight on.
Would you say the way you feel about yourself overall—your sense of confidence or self-worth—depends a lot on your weight or how your body looks?

I don't know if I'd say my whole self-worth depends on it. I mean, I take pride in my work, and I know I'm a good mechanic. But... yeah, I guess how my body feels and looks does play a big part in how I feel about myself day-to-day. If I feel lean and fast, I just feel better overall. If I feel like I'm getting heavy, it definitely drags down my mood and makes me feel like I'm losing my edge. So, it's definitely a factor.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and how that compares to what you weighed a year or so ago?

I'm not exactly sure on the numbers, to be honest. I mean, my height is what it is, but... I don't really weigh myself on a scale. I just go by how my work jeans fit and how I feel moving around the shop. 

Compared to a year ago, I know I'm definitely lighter. My belts are pulled tighter now, and I feel leaner. But as for the actual pounds... I just don't have that exact number for you.
Would you be willing to step on the scale here in the office right now so we can get your exact current weight and height?

I'd honestly rather not. I mean... I know you're just trying to get your measurements, but I just don't like getting on scales. 

Like I said, I go by how my work jeans fit and how I feel moving around. Seeing the actual number on a machine just... it bothers me. It gets in my head too much. So, no, I'd really prefer to skip that, if that's alright with you.
Besides limiting your food intake, do you ever feel driven to exercise intensely, or use any other methods like vomiting or laxatives, to control your weight?

No, I don't do any of that stuff. I mean, I don't make myself throw up, and I definitely don't take laxatives or anything like that. 

As for exercise... I work in a shop all day. I'm on my feet, lifting parts, moving around. That's a workout in itself. I don't go to a gym or run miles or anything on top of that. I just keep busy at work and watch what I eat. That's pretty much it.
Do you remember the exact height and weight numbers that were recorded during your work physical exam?

I don't remember the exact numbers they wrote on the chart, to be honest. But... that work physical is actually what got me sent here in the first place. 

The doctor doing the exam told me my weight is too low. I don't really agree with that, though. To me, I just feel lighter on my feet for basketball, and I don't feel as weighed down when I'm moving around the garage. So I didn't pay much attention to the actual numbers they were throwing around.
